notes: All required searches ran this time (7 web searches, listed in 'searches'); none found any statement by Meeks on superintelligence, extinction or existential risk, a pause or slowdown, AI safety, or self-improving AI. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538): the fastdemocracy.com bill page lists 12 cosponsors (Khanna, Mejia, Ansari, Hoyle, Lynch, Garcia, Deluzio, Grijalva, Velazquez, Ocasio-Cortez, Randall, Tonko) and Meeks is not among them; congress.gov returned HTTP 403, so the list could not be confirmed there. Earlier attempt also opened meeks.house.gov press release listing pages 1-2 and democrats-foreignaffairs.house.gov listing pages 1 and 4; pages 3-5 of meeks.house.gov were not checked. The December 2025 chip-export bill entry in 'record' comes from a search result title; that page was not opened. REVIEWER: Meeks LED the 18 September 2026 letter urging AI diplomacy with China (with Bera and Jacobs, 26 other Democrats), https://democrats-foreignaffairs.house.gov/2026/09/2026-9-meeks-bera-jacobs-lead-26-democrats-in-urging-ai-diplomacy-with-china/ . Its press release contains only the letter excerpt, no separate quote from Meeks, and a Crypto Briefing report on it (18 September 2026) also has no direct quote from him, so it is left out of statements as instructed; the excerpt says 'AI models could be used to create a deadly pathogen' and relays that Anthropic and OpenAI researchers warned the technology 'could endanger humanity'. Please decide whether leading the letter should count as his own statement, which would likely raise the grade. The 9 November press release says Meeks and Amo challenged Lutnick in January 2026 on AI chip sales to China; that page (amo.house.gov) was not opened. The Bloomberg Government article is paywalled after its opening; the quote comes from the visible opening and was read through a page-fetch tool that summarizes, so a reviewer should confirm the exact wording.
